The office will be located in the Seal Beach, Santa Barbara or San Diego office and must be able to travel up to 20% to attend site visits throughout the South Coast Region, including Santa Barbara, Ventura, Los Angeles, and Orange Counties. Travel outside the region up to 5% will also be required. The position involves using a computer keyboard and Microsoft Office software for up to eight hours per day, as well as performing office tasks that require sitting, standing, and walking between locations. The role includes coordinating and participating in meetings and conference calls, attending in\-person workgroups with stakeholders, and engaging with local, state, and federal agencies in the South Coast Region, as well as Regions 4 and 6\. Prepare technical reports including:
Biological Resource Reports

NEPA and CEQA documentation

Strong experience with:

Environmental regulatory documentation

Experience conducting biological field surveys and habitat assessments.
Excellent technical writing and analytical skills.
Strong organizational and project coordination abilities.

Business development, proposal writing, and/or client management experience

### **Job Description and Duties**


This person performs a variety of professional scientific office and field work primarily in the Southern Fisheries District comprised of Tulare, Kern, and Kings Counties, and assists the Inland Fisheries Unit Region\-wide. Department of Fish and Wildlife


JC\-525656* 

SCE Supervisor
  

SENIOR ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST (SUPERVISORY)
$10,854\.00 \- $13,493\.00 per Month

**Final Filing Date:** **8/4/2026**


### **Job Description and Duties**


Are you ready to take on a challenge and lead a dynamic team working on high\-profile environmental projects? The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) is seeking a Limited Term Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory) to oversee the Southern California Edison (SCE) workload in our Habitat Conservation Planning Program. If you are a self\-motivated individual who thrives in fast\-paced, complex work environments and is passionate about conservation and environmental protection, we want to hear from you!  

  

  

About the Role: This is a working supervisor position where you will supervise and conduct environmental review, permitting, and conservation planning functions for SCE projects. You will play a key role in ensuring compliance with the California Endangered Species Act (CESA), California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), and Lake and Streambed Alteration (LSA) agreements, working to maintain a balance between environmental protection and project progress.  

  

  

CDFW may be serving as the Lead or Responsible Agency under CEQA in order to issue permits, in this role you will initiate, execute, and manage contracts with SCE, coordinate with consultants, and oversee the preparation of critical documents. You will guide and support the issuance of permits, ensure timely completion of environmental reviews, facilitate mitigation efforts, and assess the success of conservation measures across multiple regions.  

  

  

What You Will Do:
\- Lead a team of Senior Environmental Scientist (Specialists) in environmental review, permitting, and conservation planning for SCE projects.
\- Oversee the development and certification of CEQA documents for SCE's permits, including a Master Lake and Streambed Alteration Agreement (LSAA) and possibly CESA incidental take permits for projects across Regions 4, 5, and 6\.
\- Coordinate with regional and statewide staff to ensure project goals are met on time and in compliance with environmental laws and regulations.
\- Provide leadership and mentorship to your team, fostering a collaborative environment and driving success in complex, multi\-regional projects.
  

What We Are Looking For: We need someone who can take on a challenge, manage multiple complex projects, and ensure deadlines are met while maintaining the highest standards of environmental stewardship. If you are a problem\-solver with strong leadership skills and a passion for conservation, this could be the perfect role for you!  

  

  

In order to be eligible for this position, you must either be transfer eligible or take and pass the following exam.  

Class Title: Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory)/Exam Bulletin  

  

  

**This position is posted in the following counties:** *Orange/Santa Barbara/San Diego counties*. **Please apply to each county in which you are interested in working.**  

  

**This position is a 12\-month Limited Term (LT) and may be extended up to 24 months or become permanent.**  

During this 12\-month Limited Term assignment, you will receive full health, dental, and vision benefits! You will also earn State Service and accrue monthly leave credits.  

  

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.

The office will be located in the Seal Beach, Santa Barbara or San Diego office and must be able to travel up to 20% to attend site visits throughout the South Coast Region, including Santa Barbara, Ventura, Los Angeles, and Orange Counties. Travel outside the region up to 5% will also be required. The position involves using a computer keyboard and Microsoft Office software for up to eight hours per day, as well as performing office tasks that require sitting, standing, and walking between locations. The role includes coordinating and participating in meetings and conference calls, attending in\-person workgroups with stakeholders, and engaging with local, state, and federal agencies in the South Coast Region, as well as Regions 4 and 6\. Field site visits will be necessary, and the incumbent must be able to walk on uneven, hilly terrain. As a condition of employment, the incumbent may be required to wear a uniform in accordance with CDFW’s Operations Manual (Section 12901\) during field surveys and public interactions, both within and outside the Region as directed by the supervisor. Telework is up to the discretion and approval of the supervisor and will be consistent with current telework policies.

**Company Description** **Work with Us. Change the World.**


At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.


There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.


We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

 **Job Description**  

AECOM is actively seeking a creative, highly talented Area Manager with a focus on Environmental Site Assessment and Remediation. Area Managers are responsible for overseeing the performance of a group of major programs and/or projects to assure the achievement of internal and client\-facing KPIs. The location of this position is based in California. The successful candidate will be expected to continue to be involved in and execute billable work.

***The responsibilities of this position include, but are not limited to:***

**Project Delivery:**

* Drives program performance to meet and/or exceed client satisfaction and KPIs.
* Understands and drives business performance and the attainment and exceedance of internal KPIs.
* Interacts with business leadership on governance \& risk issues to ensure risk management triggers are identified and addressed proactively.
* Develops and formulates solutions to client problems/issues.
* Participates in project reviews of major program/project dashboards/deep dives to identify issues and improve performance.
* Works to drive faster adoption of digital tools.
* Actively integrates international Enterprise Capabilities into project delivery to meet business targets and works with business leadership to manage transitions.
* Continually develops ideas for program and process improvement.
* Is directly engaged and manages high\-quality client projects.

**People:**

* Actively shares people management responsibilities for approximately 50 department staff.
* Builds, maintains, and facilitates trusting relationships with key contacts across the depth and breadth of three multinational chemical company client organizations.
* Serves as a focal point for major issue resolution and provides rapid follow\-up to address concerns.
* Participates in feedback for Project Managers to assure client satisfaction and long\-term growth.
* Develops and implements succession plans for the team and advises on the recruiting of key people to serve client needs.
* Assures project delivery employees are trained and mentored with a long\-term goal of training new project managers.
* Coaches project managers and team members on understanding business performance and internal KPIs; implements processes with Project Managers.
* Evaluates individual performance of project managers within the department.

**Business Development:**

* Works collaboratively with Client Account Manager(s), Practice Area Leaders, and Business Line Leadership to grow profitable backlog and ensure financial success of their respective client program.
* Develops budgets that allow for business development portfolio management, tracking \& optimizing wins and bookings, and project oversight.
* Leads capture strategies for key pursuits and major projects within the department, ensures those strategies yield high capture rates, and grows the business and relevant technical capabilities.

**Operations:**

* Acts as a point of escalation for project issues and makes recommendations to improve performance. This may include addressing project resourcing gaps, supporting technical issues, resolving invoicing and cash collection challenges, addressing subconsultant and vendor concerns, etc.
* Drives consistent project management practices and procedures in alignment with AECOM Project Delivery System (PDS) and Quality Management System (QMS) requirements.
* Ensures accuracy of Workload Planning Tool output for the department.
* Maintains departmental compliance with West Region Environment Pricing guidance and DOA approval framework.
* Ensures the accuracy of the department’s Salesforce pipeline data and associated Detailed Forecast data and output reports.

  

**Qualifications** **Minimum Requirements:**

* Bachelor's degree and 8 years of experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education.
* Successful candidates will have to pass a background check and a motor vehicle records check.
* US citizenship or permanent residency is required. Sponsor ship at this time or in the future will not be offered for this role.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Master's Degree preferred.
* 15 years related experience.
* California Professional Geologist or Professional Engineer
* Exceptional communication skills, both written and verbal, with the ability to clearly articulate messages to a variety of audiences.
* Ability to influence others and move toward a common vision or goal.
* Flexible and adaptable; able to work in ambiguous situations.
* Resilient and tenacious with a propensity to persevere.
* Must be a team player and able to work collaboratively with and through others.
* Acute business acumen and understanding of organizational issues and challenges
* Strong knowledge and track record in the environmental / remediation business inclusive of risk\-based strategic asset management and advocacy in multiple state jurisdictions working for an Environmental Consultant.

Job Posting: Environmental Scientist

Department of Fish and Wildlife

JC-525715

Environmental Scientist

ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST

$4,418.00 - $9,321.00 per Month

New to State candidates will be hired into the minimum salary of the classification or minimum of alternate range when applicable.

Final Filing Date: 7/31/2026

Job Description And Duties

This person performs a variety of professional scientific office and field work primarily in the Southern Fisheries District comprised of Tulare, Kern, and Kings Counties, and assists the Inland Fisheries Unit Region-wide. Incumbent independently performs fishery resource management analysis, research, surveys, investigations, and studies; writes final reports; prepares regulatory and compliance documents; prepares non-routine correspondence and answers non-routine questions from the public. Incumbent provides consultative advice to various governmental entities and agencies. Incumbent shares responsibility for the fishery on the Kern Plateau including Little Kern Golden trout, Kern River Rainbow trout, and California Golden trout.

The South District staff lead conduct fishery studies, fish rescues, fish die-off investigations, fish population surveys (i.e. visual, e-fishing, snorkeling, and/or red surveys), exotic fish species and/or aquatic invasive species removals, water quantity/quality measurements, and site visits to evaluate site specific habitat conditions. Additionally, Incumbent provides oversight for the aquatic species on the Kern Plateau and managing any associated grants or contracts.

Personal Leave Program: Effective July 1, 2025, state employees are subject to temporary salary reductions ranging from 2% to 4.62% in exchange for Personal Leave Program (PLP) hours. Please note that the salary ranges listed in this Job Control may not reflect these reductions associated with the 2025 Personal Leave Program.

Please follow the link for more information regarding the 2025 Personal Leave program:

Personal Leave Program - Human Resources - CalHR.

This position may be eligible for a telework opportunity in accordance with departmental policies and operational needs. Beginning July 1, 2026, employees will be required to work in-person at least four (4) days per week in alignment with Executive Order N-22-25. Additional in-office days may be required based on operational needs.

Link to Environmental Scientist Exam: CalCareers

This position is posted in the following counties: Fresno and Kern. Please apply to each county in which you are interested in working.

You will find additional information about the job in the Duty Statement
.

Working Conditions

Requires Incumbent To Be Able Work In Remote Mountainous Terrain, Hike Extended Distances On Multi-day Backcountry Trips. In Order To Complete The Essential Functions Of This Position The Following Activities Are Required:

Work and drive in inclement weather.
Lift at least 45 pounds.
Work flexible hours (day and night) especially during field season, including

weekends to respond to changing weather conditions, to monitor and move

equipment, and conduct field surveys.

Use a computer several hours a day which involves sitting most of the time, but may

include walking or standing for brief periods.

Travel overnight (sometimes for multiple nights) occasionally.

Minimum Requirements

You will find the Minimum Requirements in the Class Specification.

Job Description And Duties

We are seeking a dynamic and a driven leader in Riverside or Sacramento.

The California Air Resources Board’s (CARB) Office of Community Air Protection (OCAP) is seeking a highly capable and forward-looking Staff Air Pollution Specialist to join the Program Assessment and Reporting Section and help guide California’s community focused air quality work. This position offers a unique opportunity to apply advanced technical expertise and provide leadership in a program that plays a central role in supporting environmental equity across the state.

The successful candidate will bring strong analytical judgment, scientific insight, and strategic thinking to assist Section-level planning and decision making. This includes contributing to the development of Section and assisting achieve its strategic goals, supporting alignment across internal teams, and helping shape approaches that strengthen Program's effectiveness statewide.

Technical leadership is a key component of this role. The incumbent will draw on a deep understanding of air quality science and community level exposure assessment to support the development and refinement of analytical approaches used across the program. This includes interpreting diverse technical information, synthesizing complex findings, and helping ensure that analyses are clearly communicated to both technical and non-technical audiences.

The position also involves providing leadership in collaborative efforts with community partners, local agencies, and internal CARB divisions. By fostering strong communication, supporting problem solving, and identifying emerging needs, the Staff Air Pollution Specialist will help strengthen program consistency and responsiveness. Lessons learned through these interactions will inform improved practices and contribute to OCAP’s continued evolution.

The role also supports the advancement of modern digital communication tools that enhance accessibility of program information. The incumbent will utilize analytical and visualization platforms, such as ArcGIS and Microsoft Power BI, contributing to clearer communication of complex concepts and improved transparency across OCAP’s work.

This position offers an opportunity to apply strong leadership, advanced technical expertise, and collaborative skills to one of CARB’s most community driven programs, helping shape approaches that support cleaner air and healthier communities across California.

jobs.title: Environmental Health Safety Specialist
jobs.description:
The Environmental, Health & Safety (EHS) Specialist is responsible for leading and managing all EHS programs within a lithium-ion battery manufacturing environment. This is a hands-on, standalone role requiring a self-motivated professional who can independently develop, implement, and maintain safety and environmental compliance programs while supporting daily manufacturing operations. The EHS Specialist will ensure compliance with OSHA, EPA, DOT, and local regulatory requirements, with specific focus on chemical handling, lithium battery safety, hazardous waste management, and industrial risk prevention.

Key responsibilities

Serve as the primary EHS representative for the facility and the on-site safety resource.
Develop, implement, and continuously improve EHS policies, procedures, and training programs.
Promote a proactive safety culture across manufacturing, warehouse, and engineering teams.

Regulatory Compliance

Ensure full compliance with OSHA, EPA, state/local regulations, and industry best practices.
Maintain required EHS documentation including SDS management, incident logs, inspections, and permits.
Support regulatory audits and serve as the main contact for external agencies.

Manufacturing & Chemical Safety

Oversee safe handling and storage of lithium-ion battery materials, including electrolytes, solvents, and powders.
Implement controls for fire prevention, thermal runaway risks, and emergency response procedures.
Conduct job hazard analyses (JHAs) and risk assessments for production activities.

Compliance & audit readiness

Ensure document control practices support compliance with ISO 9001, AS9100 (if applicable), and internal ALE quality system requirements.
Support EHS-related documentation aligned with ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 where applicable.
Maintain controlled records in an audit-ready state with complete approval and traceability history.
Support internal, customer, and external audits by providing controlled documents and records promptly.

Hazardous Materials & Waste Management

Manage hazardous waste programs including labeling, storage, accumulation areas, and disposal coordination.
Ensure compliance with DOT requirements for shipping lithium batteries and hazardous materials (UN 3480/3481).
Coordinate environmental reporting and waste reduction initiatives.

Training & Employee Engagement

Conduct EHS onboarding and recurring training (PPE, chemical safety, lockout/tagout, emergency response, etc.).
Lead safety meetings, toolbox talks, and incident prevention initiatives.
Provide hands-on coaching to employees on safe work practices

Incident Management & Continuous Improvement

Lead investigations for near-misses, injuries, spills, or safety events.
Track corrective and preventive actions to closure.
Monitor site safety performance metrics and recommend improvements.

Emergency Preparedness

Maintain emergency response plans including fire protection, chemical spill response, evacuation procedures, and first aid readiness.
Coordinate drills and ensure emergency equipment is inspected and functional.

Daily On-the-Floor Support

Perform routine safety inspections and audits in production and warehouse areas.
Partner closely with operations leadership to address safety concerns in real time.
Support implementation of 5S and safe manufacturing practices.

Qualification

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Health & Safety, Industrial Hygiene, Environmental Science, or related field (or equivalent experience).
3+ years of EHS experience in a manufacturing or industrial environment.
Strong working knowledge of OSHA regulations and safety management systems.
Ability to work independently in a one-person EHS role and manage multiple priorities.
Experience in lithium-ion battery, chemical, electronics, or high-tech manufacturing.
Knowledge of hazardous material shipping and storage regulations (DOT/IATA).
Familiarity with ISO 14001 or ISO 45001 standards.
HAZWOPER or other relevant certifications (a plus).

Work Environment and Physical requirements

Manufacturing facility with exposure to chemicals, powered industrial equipment, and regulated battery materials.
Requires use of PPE and adherence to strict safety protocols.
May involve occasional lifting, walking production floors, and responding to urgent safety needs.
Frequent bending, squatting, reaching, and climbing.
Ability to lift up to 35 lbs.
Ability to stand and walk for extended periods.
Ability to work safely

Job Description And Duties

The Greenhouse Gas (GHG) Emissions Data Quality Assurance Section in the Program Planning and Management Branch has a vacant Air Pollution Specialist (APS) position for which it is seeking highly competent candidates with experience and expertise in natural and working lands GHG quantification and emissions reduction methods. The Section is responsible for ensuring the impartiality and quality of third-party verifications and will oversee third-party verifications performed as required by Senate Bill 27: Carbon sequestration: state goals: natural and working lands: registry of projects (SB 27).

Under direction of the Air Resources I, the APS applies scientific methods and principles in the identification, study, and solution of air pollution problems. The APS designs, conducts, and evaluates methods to reduce GHG emissions from natural and working lands. The APS specifically focuses on forests, floodplains and wetlands, coastal habitats, agriculture, and urban lands. This candidate will work in coordination with the California Natural Resources Agency to develop the Natural and Working Lands Climate Smart Strategy, as required by SB 27, and will also play a lead role in establishing carbon dioxide removal targets for 2030 and beyond, while considering the Natural and Working Lands Climate Smart Strategy, science-based data, cost-effectiveness, and technological feasibility in setting the targets.

The candidate will support CARB’s efforts in developing policy through technical and policy analysis, and quantifying the costs, benefits, and equity implications of natural and working lands policies. Additionally, the candidate will identify research needs that advance CARB’s understanding of cutting-edge issues in natural and working lands. The candidate will engage and collaborate with relevant stakeholders including, but not limited to, public agencies, research institutions, equity stakeholders, developers, industry, and other CARB staff, management, and executive leadership teams. This candidate must understand the complexities of natural and working lands and the roles that policy, technology, and the natural environment play. The candidate should also be aware of the social equity implications of natural and workin glands policies and be able to develop strategies accordingly.

jobs.title: Senior Sediment Remediation Specialist (multiple locations)
jobs.description:
**Come Work With Us**  

  

*Be Exceptional. Deliver Excellence. Make A Difference.*

LimnoTech is a leading environmental engineering and science firm with clients who face water\-related problems that are more challenging and costly than ever before. It is our job to help our clients make decisions based on the best available science and real\-world constraints.  

  

At LimnoTech, our values are to: honor the science, lead through innovation, act through partnership, commit to the long\-term, and pursue big, bold actions. Are you ready to join a team of smart, talented people who are motivated every day to deliver excellence and make a difference for our clients, our partners, and the environment?

  

LimnoTech is seeking an experienced sediment remediation specialist to lead complex environmental investigations and the design of cleanup strategies for contaminated sediment sites in riverine, lacustrine, estuarine, and marine environments. The selected candidate will be based in one of LimnoTech's primary office locations (Ann Arbor, Los Angeles, Oakdale, or DC). Come work with us!  

  

Responsibilities  

  

The Senior Sediment Remediation Specialist will lead complex environmental investigations and the design of cleanup strategies for contaminated sediment sites in riverine, lacustrine, estuarine, and marine environments. This senior role requires a seasoned professional to provide technical, managerial, regulatory, and business development support to LimnoTech’s existing contaminated sediments practice. Typical job responsibilities include the following, depending on individual ability, skills, and experience:  

* Leading and overseeing technical work for the full lifecycle of sediment projects, which may include developing site characterization, remedial investigation (RI), and feasibility study (FS) plans; overseeing multi\-media sampling programs (sediment, water, biota, etc.); data interpretation (geostatistics, fingerprinting, etc.); numerical modeling (hydrodynamic, contaminant fate and transport, etc.); developing conceptual site models; evaluating and implementing remedial alternatives (dredging, capping, MNR, etc.); remedial cost estimating; and translating complex scientific findings into high quality technical written/verbal deliverables. Litigation support and expert witness experience is desirable.
* Managing projects through the full project management life cycle, including developing scopes of work, managing budgets, leading and mentoring project teams, coordinating with multi\-disciplinary teams of scientist, engineers, regulators, and responsible parties, delivering high quality deliverables on time and on budget, and client management.
* Providing regulatory expertise on contaminated sediment projects (e.g.: CERCLA, RCRA, or local state programs), which may include agency negotiations.
* Leading and participating in marketing and business development activities, which may include tracking and pursuing relevant requests for proposals, developing marketing documents (quals packages, project profiles, web articles, etc.), cultivating and nurturing client and partner relationships, and actively participating at relevant conferences (e.g.: Battelle).

  

Qualifications  

  

The ideal candidate will possess a minimum of a Bachelor of Science degree in Civil or Environmental Engineering, Geology, Environmental Science, or a closely related physical science discipline with 10 or more years of experience in the field. A Master’s degree or Ph.D. is strongly preferred, as the role demands a deep understanding of complex contaminant transport, sediment geochronology, and geochemical partitioning.
* For engineering applicants, an active Professional Engineer (PE) license is expected; for scientists, a Professional Geologist (PG) or related credentials would be highly valued, demonstrating a commitment to professional standards and the ability to seal technical documents.
* In addition to formal academic credentials, specialized training in hydrodynamic modeling or statistical data analysis is a significant advantage.
* Candidates must also have completed the 40\-hour OSHA HAZWOPER certification with current annual refreshers, ensuring they are qualified to oversee field activities at hazardous waste sites.
* Continuous education through participation in industry organizations, such as the Battelle Sediment Conference or ITRC technical teams, is encouraged to ensure the firm remains at the forefront of emerging remediation technologies and evolving regulatory frameworks.
* A demonstrated interest or experience in urban waterfront restoration, engineering with nature, or nature\-based solutions is a plus.
* Must be legally able to work in the U.S. for any employer (proper documentation is required).

  

Compensation  

  

LimnoTech rewards high achievement within a supportive working community. Individual achievement is rewarded through a unique merit review process based on recommendations from colleagues at all levels of the company, plus positive feedback from clients. This system drives pay increases and opportunities for increased project and corporate responsibility. We track individual progress annually to ensure competitiveness within our industry and identify opportunities for targeted professional development. The salary for this position will be determined based on the candidate’s years and type of experience, degrees earned, office location, and fit with job requirements, and is expected to range between $110,000 and $200,000 annually.

The role will include negotiating with regulatory agencies to resolve compliance issues and secure necessary permits. The role will develop advanced tools and standards to support compliance efforts and mitigate environmental liabilities. Review technical work performed by more junior staff.
Conduct regulatory gap analysis to pinpoint areas requiring increased compliance.
Develop strategic permit plans and prepare permit applications.
Prepare permit application forms, ensuring all information required by regulatory agencies is included.
Conduct multi-media environmental audits, assessments, and reporting for comprehensive environment management.
Support compliance and reporting activities, ensuring all relevant documentation is prepared and submitted on time.
Support development of compliance programs.
Negotiate with agencies, acting as the primary point of contact for all environmental issues.
Mitigate environmental liability and risk through strategic planning and risk management.
Advance and implement tools and standards for environmental compliance and permitting.
Flexibility to adapt and execute various additional assignments based on evolving needs.

Mentorship

Provide mentorship, guidance, support, and knowledge-sharing to help less experienced team members develop their skills and grow within their roles.

Skills and Competencies

Expertise in regulatory gap analysis and strategic permit planning.
Advanced competency in preparing permit applications and conducting environmental audits and assessments.
Strong thought leadership abilities and skills in compliance support, reporting, and agency negotiations.
Proficient in written and oral communications with clients.

Experience

Extensive experience in environmental liability management, risk reduction, and development of tools and standards.

The Greenhouse Gas (GHG) Emissions Data Quality Assurance Section in the Program Planning and Management Branch has a vacant Air Pollution Specialist (APS) position for which it is seeking highly competent candidates with experience and expertise in natural and working lands GHG quantification and emissions reduction methods. The Section is responsible for ensuring the impartiality and quality of third\-party verifications and will oversee third\-party verifications performed as required by Senate Bill 27: Carbon sequestration: state goals: natural and working lands: registry of projects (SB 27\).  

Under direction of the Air Resources I, the APS applies scientific methods and principles in the identification, study, and solution of air pollution problems. The APS designs, conducts, and evaluates methods to reduce GHG emissions from natural and working lands. The APS specifically focuses on forests, floodplains and wetlands, coastal habitats, agriculture, and urban lands. This candidate will work in coordination with the California Natural Resources Agency to develop the Natural and Working Lands Climate Smart Strategy, as required by SB 27, and will also play a lead role in establishing carbon dioxide removal targets for 2030 and beyond, while considering the Natural and Working Lands Climate Smart Strategy, science\-based data, cost\-effectiveness, and technological feasibility in setting the targets.  

The candidate will support CARB’s efforts in developing policy through technical and policy analysis, and quantifying the costs, benefits, and equity implications of natural and working lands policies. Additionally, the candidate will identify research needs that advance CARB’s understanding of cutting\-edge issues in natural and working lands. The candidate will engage and collaborate with relevant stakeholders including, but not limited to, public agencies, research institutions, equity stakeholders, developers, industry, and other CARB staff, management, and executive leadership teams. This candidate must understand the complexities of natural and working lands and the roles that policy, technology, and the natural environment play. jobs.description:
**About EHS Support**

  

EHS Support is a specialty environmental consulting firm that provides solutions to complex environmental, health, and safety challenges across a range of market sectors and industries. With experts located throughout the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, the United Kingdom, and South Africa, we form long\-lasting partnerships with our clients through a culture of excellence, innovation, work ethic, and integrity. We focus on hiring and retaining talented, motivated people who enjoy collaborating with and delivering value to our clients. Our team does more than identify problems— we provide solutions.

 **Location:** Brisbane, QLD \- flexible home, office and field\-based role

**About the Role**


We are seeking an experienced environmental scientist or engineer to join our Queensland team and play a leading role in the delivery of environmental assessment, compliance, remediation and environmental management projects.


This role is suited to an experienced consultant who enjoys technical problem solving, project leadership and working with clients to develop practical and defensible environmental solutions. The position offers exposure to a broad range of projects and sectors, including energy, resources, infrastructure, manufacturing, chemicals and heavy industry.


While a strong background in contaminated land assessment and management is important, we are particularly interested in adaptable practitioners who can apply their technical skills across a range of environmental disciplines, including compliance, approvals, environmental due diligence, environmental management and remediation.


The preferred location for this role is Brisbane; however, other Queensland locations will be considered for suitably experienced candidates. The role involves a flexible mix of office, home and field\-based work, together with periodic travel to project sites throughout Queensland and Australia.

**Typical responsibilities:**

* Lead technical delivery of environmental assessment, compliance, remediation and environmental management projects.
* Plan, coordinate and manage environmental investigations, including soil, groundwater, surface water and vapour assessment programs.
* Review, interpret and evaluate environmental data and develop technically robust and commercially practical recommendations.
* Author and review technical reports and project deliverables, including:


 o Preliminary and detailed site investigations


 o Contaminated land assessments


 o Remediation action plans and validation reports


 o Environmental management plans


 o Compliance and monitoring report


 o Environmental approvals and supporting documentation

* Provide technical leadership and quality assurance for work completed by project team members.
* Lead the technical delivery and project execution of environmental assessment, compliance, remediation and environmental management projects.
* Coordinate and supervise subcontractors and specialist service providers during field investigations and remediation works.
* Engage directly with clients, regulators, contractors and other stakeholders to support project delivery and resolve technical issues.
* Contribute to proposal preparation, scope development and cost estimation for new opportunities.
* Support the development of junior and intermediate staff through technical guidance, coaching and project leadership.
* Contribute to technical innovation and continuous improvement initiatives within the business.


As a growing business, this role provides opportunities to expand technical leadership responsibilities, strengthen client relationships, contribute to service development and play a meaningful role in the continued growth of the Queensland practice.

**Position Requirements:**


This opportunity is suited to a motivated and adaptable environmental professional who combines strong technical capability with project leadership and client management skills. The successful candidate will demonstrate:

* Strong technical knowledge of contaminated land assessment, remediation and environmental management principles.
* Excellent analytical and critical\-thinking skills, with the ability to develop practical and defensible solutions to complex environmental challenges.
* Exceptional written communication skills and demonstrated experience preparing high\-quality technical reports and client deliverables.
* Strong verbal communication and stakeholder engagement skills.
* Proven ability to manage projects, coordinate multidisciplinary teams and deliver successful outcomes.
* Ability to work independently while providing leadership and direction within collaborative project teams.
* Sound professional judgement and a practical approach to balancing technical, regulatory and commercial considerations.
* A strong commitment to health, safety and environmental performance.

**Qualifications for this role include:**

* Bachelor's or Master's degree in Soil Science, Geology, Hydrogeology, Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering or a related discipline.
* Approximately 7\-10 years' experience in environmental consulting or a closely related technical role.
* Demonstrated experience undertaking and managing contaminated land investigations, environmental site assessments and remediation projects.
* Strong understanding of the ASC NEPM and Queensland contaminated land regulatory framework.
* Experience managing environmental field programs, including soil, groundwater and surface water investigations.
* Demonstrated experience leading the preparation and review of high\-quality technical reports and client deliverables.
* Proven project management experience, including management of scope, schedule, budget and project risks.
* Experience working across multiple environmental service areas such as compliance, approvals, environmental management, due diligence or remediation would be highly regarded.
* Current Australian drive

ERM is a global environmental consultancy with one of the largest group of air quality specialists in Australia. Our projects (in Australia and overseas) include impact assessment and mitigation, air quality monitoring, air quality assessment, dispersion modelling, odour and dust assessment, emissions inventory development, carbon management, applied meteorology, and regulatory reporting.

If you are a highly motivated and results-orientated person looking to make your mark in a leading environmental consultancy, then we would like to hear from you!

Deliver emission estimation inventories, odour and air quality modelling assessments;
Write technical environmental reports, effective proposals, and tenders;
Plan projects with a range of complexity and scale;
Achieve client’s expectations for scope, budget, schedule, and quality;
Lead client-focused air permitting and compliance strategies for industrial facilities, addressing complex regulatory and technical issues while maintaining strong client relationships and supporting operational flexibility;
Develop and expand client relationships that support repeat business, identifying and developing new opportunities;
Capitalize on existing client relationships to expand ERM’s profile and market share in the regional air quality market (through a combination of excellence in technical delivery and business development);
Mentor team members in the proper planning and execution of air quality projects, and conduct independent technical reviews of deliverable work products;
Support the general growth and development of ERM’s global air quality services;
Collaborate with other ERM global practitioners to execute air quality projects.

8+ years of relevant experience in air quality/compliance consulting.
Well established reputation and recognized technical expertise by the marketplace.

jobs.description:
**Position Information**
------------------------


**We are seeking an Environmental Health Specialist II to join the Department of Health Services and help advance the health and safety of Sonoma County!**

**Starting salary up to $60\.53/hour ($126,333/year) and a competitive total compensation package!\***


The Department of Health Services is currently recruiting to fill one full\-time Environmental Health Specialist (EHS) position at either the Trainee, I, or II level. If you are interested in being considered at the different levels of this opportunity, you must apply to the separate concurrent recruitments being conducted for each level.

**Please Note:** As mandated by the State of California's Health and Safety Code, the Environmental Health Specialist II level requires possession of a valid certificate of registration as an Environmental Health Specialist. For more information on the requirements and process to obtain a Registered Environmental Health Specialist certificate in California, please visit the CA Registered Environmental Health Specialist Program website.  

  

**About the Position**
We're looking for a motivated individual to join our team as an Environmental Health Specialist II who wants to advance their career in Environmental Health. This role is vital to protecting public health, serving the community, and supporting the functions of the Environmental Health Section. As an Environmental Health Specialist II, you will:

* Perform inspections and investigations across a wide range of programs, including but not limited to: Food Facilities, Recreational Facilities, Cannabis Facilities, Medical Waste Facilities, Water Systems, Beach monitoring, Solid Waste, Body Art, Childhood Lead Prevention, Storm Water, Organized Camps, Detention Facilities, and Disaster Preparedness
* Ensure compliance with County and State health and safety regulations through routine inspections, complaint responses, documentation, enforcement actions, and public education
* Prepare thorough inspection reports, interpret relevant health codes, and communicate findings and corrective actions to stakeholders
* Interact regularly with the public, businesses, and regulatory partners, often providing guidance and support in diverse environments
* Be a subject matter expert for the work of the program they are assigned to

  

As the ideal candidate for this position, you will be dedicated to helping promote a healthy and safe environment, be an excellent communicator, and possess many of the following:* Experience with sanitation science, public health principles, and relevant environmental health laws and regulations
* The ability to adapt to an evolving public health landscape and perform a broad range of functions to meet Departmental operational needs
* Experience identifying potential issues, researching these issues, preparing supporting documentation, and presenting these observations accurately and effectively
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint) and general computer skills
* Effective written and verbal communication skills, including report writing, documentation, and presentations
* The ability to think critically, research regulatory issues, and analyze field findings
* A strong sense of empathy for the clients you will work with
* The ability to build collaborative relationships with a diverse community, team members, and partner agencies

  

Work is primarily performed Monday through Friday, with occasional evenings and weekends to inspect temporary events or respond to complaints. Many inspections are outdoors and require working in varying environmental conditions, including beaches, waste sites, and food service facilities.

**What We Offer**


Working at the County of Sonoma offers expansive opportunities for growth and development, the ability to be a part of a challenging and rewarding work environment, and the satisfaction of knowing you're working to better our communities. You can also look forward to flexible work arrangements and excellent benefits\* including:

* **Salary Advancement** \- A salary increase after 1,040 hours (6 months when working full\-time) for good work performance; eligibility for a salary increase for good performance every year thereafter, until reaching the top of the salary range
* **Paid Time Off** \- Competitive vacation and sick leave accruals and 12 paid holidays
* **County Paid Health Premium Contributions** \- 100% premium contribution for the majority of employee\-only and employee \+ family health plan options
* **Staff Development/Wellness** \- Annual benefit allowances of up to $850 and ongoing education/training opportunities
* **Post\-Retirement Health Reimbursement Arrangement** \- County contributions to help fund post\-retirement health insurance/benefits
* **Retirement** \- A pension fully integrated with Social Security
* **Paid Parental Leave** \- May be eligible for up to 8 weeks (320 hours) after 12 months of County employment
* **Additional Benefits** \- Excellent dental, vision, disability, life insurance, employee assistance program, professional development, and more
* **Student Loan Debt Relief** \- County employees may be eligible for Public Service Loan Forgiveness through the U.S. Department of Education
* Salary is negotiable within the established range. Benefits described herein do not represent a contract and may be changed without notice. Additional information can be found in the Engineers and Scientists of California Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) and our Employee Benefits Directory.


This recruitment is being conducted to fill an Environmental Health Specialist II position in the Department of Health Services. This employment list may also be used to fill future full\-time, part\-time, or extra\-help (temporary) positions as they occur during the active status of the list.

**Application submissions require the Supplemental Questionnaire to be completed.**

**Final Filing Date:** **8/1/2026**


### **Job Description and Duties**


Do you have a desire to work to reduce waste and help protect the health and well\-being of California’s people and environment? Do you have the knowledge and skills to perform scientific, analytical and technical work to help affected parties achieve "compliance through assistance"?  

  

In the Local Assistance and Market Development Branch (LAMD) staff are CalRecycle’s field representatives, delivering the department's vision to inspire and challenge Californians to achieve the highest waste reduction, recycling, and reuse goals in the nation. Additionally, staff play an important role in delivering the department's services and programs to local and regional jurisdictions and providing technical assistance for building comprehensive recycling communities.  

  

Staff play a key role in assisting local governments, local education agencies, and non local entities such as state and federal agencies in achieving statutorily mandated waste diversion goals; educating, motivating and overseeing programs to increase public participation in all aspects of waste reduction, including waste prevention, recycling, and composting in addition to edible food recovery. In addition, the staff is responsible for participating on collaborative teams focused on the department’s high\-priority initiatives. This position involves travel throughout the state approximately 20% of the time.  

  

This position is currently telework centric under California Government Code 14200 for eligible applicants residing in California, and occasionally reports to headquarters for hands on meetings and/or trainings. jobs.description:
**Job Overview:**



APTIM Environmental \& Infrastructure, LLC is seeking a mid\-level Environmental Scientist on a full\-time basis to work remotely from Oregon to participate in a variety of environmental compliance tasks in support of environmental compliance and permitting review programs. The successful candidate will prepare technical and compliance reports and review reports completed by other personnel, and lead training of other staff members. Assist in preparation of proposals, budgets, vendor/subcontractor selection, and other contract related items. Conduct technical and regulatory analyses and review analyses of junior personnel. Perform diverse fieldwork, possibly including sampling inspections and audits. Apply expertise to both standard and unique situations, ensuring environmental standards are met across projects. Be expected to maintain current knowledge of environmental regulations and emerging developments. This role requires both independent work and collaboration with multidisciplinary teams to ensure compliance and provide clients with practical, science\-based solutions. Responsibilities may also include supervising junior staff and participating in leadership development opportunities. This position will primarily be remote but may also require travel to client facilities, conduct environmental compliance reviews/audits and/or gather related data.


**Key Responsibilities/Accountabilities:**


* Executing and managing various work scopes, while meeting project schedules and budgets.
* Collection and interpretation/evaluation of scientific data.
* Executes field work within project schedule and budgetary goals and supervises subcontractors.
* Use various environmental databases and software to research project/site requirements and document the results in a technical report.
* Work independently and as part of a project team and be able to adjust to changing conditions or client requirements. Supervises junior staff on more complex work tasks.
* Adheres to established health and safety policies and procedures and executes work in a safe and conscientious manner.
* Understands technical concepts, evaluation results, plans, reports, and ensures conformance to applicable technical standards.
* Interfacing with client personnel at a corporate and facility level.
* Has in\-depth experience, knowledge, and skills in own discipline.
* Flexible and willing to support other projects as needed.
* Drafts technical documents for regulatory agencies and private clients.
* Providing training, guidance and oversight to junior staff.
* Applies knowledge and skills to more complex situations.
* Build and maintain successful client relationships.
* Work with clients to evaluate proposed projects for anticipated impacts, define type of environmental requirements needed and prepare proposals.
* Communications with regulatory agencies.
* Time management to ensure a quality product is prepared to meet project deadlines.
* Applies knowledge and skills to a wide range of standard and nonstandard situations.
* Following defined processes explicitly while also being able to identify and accommodate new or changing scenarios as well as developing processes for new activities.
* Prior experience or training regarding environmental compliance and related federal and state environmental regulations required.
* Experience with auditing is preferred.


**Basic Qualifications:**


* Bachelor's degree in environmental science, a core science (such as geology, chemistry, physics, or biology), engineering, or related area required.
* Related work experience of 4\-6 years.
* Must have strong written and oral communication skills.
* Must have strong organizational skills.
* Strong computer skills required. Must have demonstrated strength and proficiency with Microsoft applications such as MS Excel, MS Word, SharePoint Online, and ability to learn other software applications.
* May be asked to work in the field and travel to complete work.


**About APTIM**



APTIM enhances the quality of the environment, wellbeing of people, resilience of communities, and opportunity for employees to make a difference, not just a living. A leading professional solutions firm, we specialize in environmental, sustainability, resilience, and infrastructure solutions. Our team of experts provide these integrated solutions for forward\-thinking government agencies, commercial and industrial clients, and energy customers. Together, we create sustainable and resilient communities for all.



What you can expect from APTIM:


* Work that is worthy of your time and talent
* Respect and flexibility to live a full life at work and at home
* Dogged determination to deliver for our clients and communities
* A voice in making our company better
* Investment into your personal and professional development


As of the date of this posting, a good faith estimate of the current pay range for this position is $80,000 to $85,000 per year. Compensation depends on several factors including: experience, education, key skills, geographic location of the position, client requirements, external market competitiveness, and internal equity among other employees within APTIM.


**Employee Benefits**


APTIM Environmental \& Infrastructure, llp committed to providing an extensive range of benefits that protect and promote the health and financial well\-being of our employees and their families through the APTIM Benefits Marketplace https://aptim.makeityoursource.com/.


* Medical, vision, and dental insurance: Through the marketplace, our employees can choose benefits from five metallic levels and several carriers to find the right benefits that work for them in their location.
* Company paid and optional Life insurance
* Short\-term and long\-term disability insurance
* Accident, Critical Illness, and Hospital Indemnity coverage
* Paid holidays, vacation, and sick leave (eligibility based on company policy and applicable law)
* 401(k) APTIM of

jobs.title: Chemical Regulatory Manager
jobs.description:
RED Digital Cinema, a Nikon Group company,
is a leading manufacturer of professional digital cameras. RED's modular camera system and groundbreaking image quality are by far the best on the market today! Started by Jim Jannard (founder of Oakley), RED continues to break ground with new products like KOMODO and V-RAPTOR. RED was used for major productions like The Queen's Gambit, The Social Dilemma, My Octopus Teacher, The Suicide Squad, The Morning Show, Russian Doll, Squid Game, Matrix, Red Notice, and Mank. In addition, RED has been selected as the camera of choice in 3 major productions, winning 2 Oscars and 3 Emmys in the cinematography category.

RED Digital Cinema is seeking a Chemical Regulatory Manager who will be responsible for ensuring compliance with global chemical regulations and Chemical Management Systems (CMS). This role oversees regulatory strategy, product compliance, hazard communication, and chemical risk management to ensure adherence to applicable local, regional, and international regulations. The position partners cross-functionally with R&D, Quality, Supply Chain, and Manufacturing to support product development, market access, and ongoing regulatory compliance.

Key Responsibilities include:
Regulatory Compliance & Strategy

Develop and implement chemical regulatory strategies to ensure compliance with global chemical regulations (e.g., REACH, TSCA, RoHS, Prop 65, etc.)
Monitor regulatory changes and assess impact on products and operations
Lead chemical registration, notification, and reporting activities across relevant jurisdictions
Maintain regulatory documentation and compliance records

Chemical Management System (CMS) Oversight

Develop, maintain, and continuously improve the company’s Chemical Management System
Ensure proper classification, labeling, and Safety Data Sheet (SDS) management
Support internal audits and regulatory inspections

Product Stewardship

Conduct chemical risk assessments and hazard evaluation
Collaborate with R&D during product development to ensure regulatory compliance
Evaluate raw materials and supplier documentation for compliance risk
Provide regulatory guidance on product changes and new formulations
Managing EPR compliance for WEEE/EEE (e-waste), batteries, packaging, and other international environmental obligations

Cross-Functional Collaboration

Partner with internal teams to ensure regulatory alignment
Support customer and supplier regulatory inquiries
Train internal stakeholders on chemical regulatory requirements
Serve as primary contact for regulatory authorities as needed

Documentation & Reporting

Prepare and submit regulatory filings and reports
Ensure accurate hazard communication (labels, SDS, technical documentation)
Maintain compliance databases and reporting tools

Qualifications
Education

Bachelor’s degree in Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Environmental Science, Regulatory Affairs, or related field

Experience

10+ years of experience in chemical regulatory affairs or compliance
Strong knowledge of global chemical regulations
Experience managing chemical registrations and regulatory submissions
Experience with chemical compliance software or CMS platforms

Skills & Competencies

Strong analytical and risk assessment skills
Excellent written and verbal communication skills
Ability to interpret complex regulatory language
Strong project management and organizational skills
Leadership experience preferred

Preferred Certifications
Regulatory Affairs Certification (RAC)
Certified Chemical Professional (CCP)

jobs.description:
Environmental Specialist

Triumvirate Environmental, one of the largest environmental services firms in North America, is seeking an Environmental Specialist for our
Lab & Onsite Support Services (Lab/OSS)
team. As an Environmental Specialist, you will support our clients on-site by managing their hazardous waste programs & projects, utilizing state & federal regulations.  
Triumvirate Environmental provides leading organizations in the higher education, life sciences, healthcare, and advanced manufacturing sectors with diverse services and expertise to assist them with compliance management. At Triumvirate Environmental, we strive to WOW both our employees and our customers. Our unique culture fosters growth, development, education, and creativity.    
This position reports to the Program Manager. This role is based on site at a client location in  South San Francisco
, CA
along with other locations throughout  the Bay area.
We invite you to watch this video to discover more about the exciting responsibilities of an Environmental Specialist at Triumvirate Environmental.
CLICK HERE

Responsibilities:

Develop an understanding of OSHA regulations as well as Triumvirate’s Health and Safety practices 
Preparation of chemical and biological waste for shipment and disposal, including creation of all federal/state waste documents and managing the paperwork for the material. 
Safe handling of hazardous waste containers on client sites, as well as loading/unloading of waste from vehicles 
Conduct safety equipment and hazardous waste inspections. 
Occasionally perform and document Environmental Health and Safety (EHS) audits for clients. 
Deliver Exceptional Customer Service: Champion our commitment to the WOW! by providing outstanding support and innovative solutions to our clients 
Develop a high-level of state and federal regulatory expertise ensuring our client’s compliance needs are met (e.g RCRA, DOT, and OSHA) 
Conduct spill response measures, including the assessment of the spills and cleanup efforts 
Rotating on-call responsibilities as part of our Emergency Response team (optional)

Basic Requirements
:  
Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience in the hazardous-waste industry, or relevant military experience 
Ability to work as a member of a team as well as individually 
Must demonstrate strong verbal and written communication abilities to effectively interact with clients, colleagues, and stakeholders, ensuring clear and professional exchanges of information 
Demonstrated ability to analyze complex issues, develop solutions, and implement strategies to achieve positive outcomes 
Skilled in building strong, positive relationships with clients and colleagues 
Ability to work overtime on a regular basis 
Must be willing to work flexible hours within the work week (Monday through Friday) 
Ability to complete a 2 to 3 year professional advancement program in hazardous waste management 
The Environmental Specialist frequently handles hazardous chemicals and biological waste and is responsible for putting on and taking off personal protective equipment. This role is considered safety-sensitive 
Must be able to report to the San Leandro office within 1 hour during Emergency Response rotating shifts  

Valid US driver’s license 
Must have a reliable form of transportation 
Must be willing to consent to Motor Vehicle Record screening, criminal background check, pre-employment physical, and drug screen (inclusive of THC) 
Upon employment, you will be required to participate in a random drug screening program (inclusive of THC) as part of our company’s commitment to maintaining a safe and healthy work environment 
Must be eligible to work in the United States without future sponsorship 
Must be able to lift 60 pounds on a regular basis 

Preferred Requirements:

Prior relevant industry experience 
Prior successful experience in a customer service role 
Active HAZWOPER 24 or 40 hour certification 

Besides Health, Dental and Vision Insurance, we contribute to a 401k, offer a generous tuition reimbursement program, TONS of safety training for some positions with opportunities for external trainings and certifications, Mentorship & Career Succession Planning, Relocation Opportunities, Auto/Home insurance discounts, pet assistance discount plans, discounted movie passes & more!    
To learn more about our business, culture, and the exciting work that we are doing in the industry, find us on LinkedIn, Instagram (@triumvirateenvironmental), or our website !   
Triumvirate Environmental is committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace. As an Equal Opportunity Employer (EOE), Triumvirate does not discriminate based on race, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, or other legally protected status. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. Individuals with Disabilities and Protected Veterans are encouraged to apply.  
If you have a disability and need accommodation during the application and hiring process, please contact us at https://www.triumvirate.com/contact or call us at 888-834-9697.  The requirements listed above are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Department Information

California’s Department of Resources Recycling and Recovery (CalRecycle) brings together the state’s recycling and waste management programs to move the state towards a circular economy that reduces waste and reuses all materials.

Through landmark initiatives like the Integrated Waste Management Act and Beverage Container Recycling and Litter Reduction Act, California works toward a society that uses less, recycles more, and takes resource conservation to higher and higher levels.

CalRecycle’s Mission: Protecting California’s environment and climate for the health and prosperity of future generations through the reduction, reuse and recycling of California resources, environmental education, disaster recovery and the transition from a disposable to a fully circular economy.

CalRecycle values diversity, equity, and inclusion throughout the organization. We foster an environment where employees from a variety of backgrounds, cultures, and personal experiences are welcomed and can thrive. We believe the diversity of our employees is essential to inspiring innovative solutions. Together we further our mission to protect the environment and preserve resources by empowering Californians to reduce, reuse, and recycle. Join CalRecycle to improve the lives of all Californians.

Department Website: http://www.calrecycle.ca.gov

Job Description And Duties

Do you have a desire to work to reduce waste and help protect the health and well-being of California’s people and environment? Do you have the knowledge and skills to perform scientific, analytical and technical work to help affected parties achieve "compliance through assistance"?

In the Local Assistance and Market Development Branch (LAMD) staff are CalRecycle’s field representatives, delivering the department's vision to inspire and challenge Californians to achieve the highest waste reduction, recycling, and reuse goals in the nation. Additionally, staff play an important role in delivering the department's services and programs to local and regional jurisdictions and providing technical assistance for building comprehensive recycling communities.

Staff play a key role in assisting local governments, local education agencies, and non local entities such as state and federal agencies in achieving statutorily mandated waste diversion goals; educating, motivating and overseeing programs to increase public participation in all aspects of waste reduction, including waste prevention, recycling, and composting in addition to edible food recovery. In addition, the staff is responsible for participating on collaborative teams focused on the department’s high-priority initiatives. This position involves travel throughout the state approximately 20% of the time.

This position is currently telework centric under California Government Code 14200 for eligible applicants residing in California, and occasionally reports to headquarters for hands on meetings and/or trainings. The position provides a mix of independent and team-oriented field work, research, analysis, report writing and correspondence.

This position requires that you possess and maintain a valid California Drivers License (CDL). You must answer the questions addressing your CDL on your applications. Ensure you provide your CDL number, class, expiration date, and any endorsements and/or restrictions. Failing to maintain a valid CDL will result in a failure to meet job requirements.

Beginning July 1, 2026, CalRecycle staff will be office-centered, requiring employees to report to the office at least four days per week. This position may be eligible for hybrid telework under Government Code 14200, subject to the candidate meeting telework eligibility criteria set forth in the CalEPA telework policy and/or future program needs. Employees not residing in California are not eligible for telework. Regardless of telework eligibility, all employees may be required to report to the positions designated headquarter location, as reflected on the duty statement and at their own expense.

.

Applications will be screened and only the most qualified applicants will be selected to move forward in the selection process. Applicants must meet the Minimum Qualifications stated in the Classification Specification(s).
